first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service for weddings in the US and Canada. They give you an advisor and say they check the legal rules. The Hawaii line about no residency rule and no waiting period jumped out straight away because the paperwork is exactly what I'm worried about. Nothing up top tells me if a tiny wedding is welcome though; 'from the first enquiry to the last dance' sounds like a big reception.

attention_map.quote: Hawaii is the simplest legal example: no residency rule, and no waiting period once your licence is issued.
attention_map.why: First thing that speaks to my worry about documents. 'we check them for your date and passports' is the line I wanted.

attention_map.quote: How many guests? Just the two of you / Up to 30
attention_map.why: This is the first real sign small is OK. Seeing 'Just the two of you' as an option made me feel I'm not wasting their time.

attention_map.quote: Legal and entry rules from official government sites, checked October 2026.
attention_map.why: Fine, reassuring that it's from official sites, but I scrolled past.

attention_map.quote: A second-line parade walking your guests through New Orleans.
attention_map.why: Pretty, but it's all about guests, long estate dinners and parades. That's the big production I'm trying to avoid. Lake Louise and Big Island caught me for a second.

attention_map.quote: Las Vegas suits a quick, glamorous ceremony; Nevada sets its own licence rules, and your Wedded Advisor checks them before you book flights.
attention_map.why: Vegas and Banff are on my list. Good that they say they check Nevada before flights, but it's still 'we'll check', nothing concrete about what I'd need.

attention_map.quote: Kauai | Sea cliffs and gardens | ... | Intimate weddings and elopements
attention_map.why: I scanned the fit column for 'small' and found Kauai, Big Sur and Las Vegas 'Couples and small groups'. That's how I read pages. Banff only says 'couples in winter', so it's a maybe. On a phone a five-column table will be hard work.

attention_map.quote: Apply online and pay, then meet a State-authorised agent together, in person, with government photo ID. A passport is accepted; proxies are not.
attention_map.why: Clear steps with the Department of Health linked. This is what I came for. But it never says whether we need witnesses, and that's one of my first questions.

attention_map.section: s3 Every other state and province
attention_map.quote: Each US state and each Canadian province sets its own licence rules. Your Wedded Advisor checks the current steps with the issuing office for your date.
attention_map.why: For Banff and Vegas, that's all I get. I'd have liked at least what documents to start gathering.

attention_map.quote: Check ESTA eligibility on the official US site before flying to the US
attention_map.why: Useful later, not why I'm here today.
That's literally how I feel, so I noticed it, but it just links off to other articles.

attention_map.quote: A Great Gatsby wedding in Vancouver
attention_map.why: Ballrooms, Gatsby, cultural celebrations. None of these looks like a small elopement, so it doesn't show me people like us.

attention_map.quote: Family gathering: a Maui stay that brings every generation together.
Sort the legal and travel steps. We check the licence rules for your state or province and the entry rules for every passport in your group.
attention_map.why: This is the 'help with everything' I want: one contact, legal sorted. Step 5 about a guest website and rooms is for bigger groups, but fine.

attention_map.quote: How to pull off a Las Vegas wedding
attention_map.why: The Vegas article title caught my eye, the rest I scrolled past.

attention_map.quote: Where can I get married with just the two of us? Hawaii is a strong choice for just the two of you ... Choose "Just the two of you" in the form and we plan around it.
attention_map.why: This answer is the one that made me feel welcome. It's buried in the FAQ though, near the bottom of a long page on my phone.

attention_map.quote: A realistic budget depends on four things: the place, the season, your guest count and how far your guests fly.
attention_map.why: No number at all, not even a minimum. I have to ask to find out.

attention_map.quote: Elopements and small weddings are welcome. A Wedded Advisor replies.
attention_map.why: Exactly the sentence I was looking for, and 'Elopement' is a choice under what we're celebrating. I wish I'd seen this near the top.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: Small groups are clearly welcome: 'Just the two of you' and 'Up to 30' options, 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome', table rows 'Intimate weddings and elopements'. No smaller package or elopement option is described anywhere, and the FAQ says Hawaii weddings are 'not usually all-inclusive'.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: Hawaii steps are spelt out with the Department of Health linked, and 'We check the licence rules for your state or province'. Witnesses are not mentioned anywhere. For Banff and Las Vegas it is only 'Rules set by Alberta / Nevada; we check them for your date'. UK documents to show 'free to marry' are mentioned, nothing for Australians.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: Budget FAQ lists drivers only: 'Share your guest count and month in the form'. No minimum anywhere.

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: Nothing on religious or church ceremonies. Only that a Hawaii officiant 'must hold a licence from the State of Hawaii Department of Health'.

objections_triggered.objection: Legal requirements abroad are confusing: outside Hawaii I'm told nothing concrete
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Every other state and province: 'Your Wedded Advisor checks the current steps with the issuing office for your date.' Witnesses never mentioned, even for Hawaii.

objections_triggered.objection: Page reads at big-group scale in the middle sections
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Spotlight 'long estate dinners', 'second-line parade walking your guests', real weddings of ballrooms and Gatsby themes, 'Plan the guest experience' with rooms and a guest website.
No line anywhere on church or Catholic weddings.

objections_triggered.objection: Nothing about being close to an airport or keeping travel simple
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No travel time or airport info; the compare table has no flights column.

trust_signals_noticed: A small-group option: 'Just the two of you' and 'Up to 30' in the guest count, 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome' above the form
Clear legal steps with an official source: Hawaii Department of Health linked, 'Last checked October 2026'
One contact: 'Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact'
Honest about rules varying rather than making things up
turn_offs_noticed: Minimum spend not stated; budget answer pushes you to the form
Real weddings and spotlight lean to big guest lists and productions

emotional_response.overall: Relieved on the Hawaii paperwork, welcomed once I found the elopement lines, a bit uneasy that the price and the Banff and Vegas rules wait for the call.
emotional_response.strongest_positive: 'Choose "Just the two of you" in the form and we plan around it.'
emotional_response.strongest_negative: The budget answer with no number.

payload.decision_reason: My threshold is met, just. Small is clearly welcome ('Just the two of you', 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome') and they say they handle the legal side, with real Hawaii steps from the Department of Health. I'd enquire picking Elopement and Just the two of you, and ask about witnesses, Banff and Vegas paperwork and a Catholic ceremony. Known gaps: no minimum spend or price shown, which nearly made me save it for later instead.
payload.verbatim_reaction: OK, the Hawaii bit is actually useful, no waiting period, passport is fine, they link the government page. But I had to scroll a long way on my phone to see 'elopements and small weddings are welcome', and in between it's parades, estate dinners and Gatsby ballrooms. Banff and Vegas just say 'we check'. Nothing about witnesses, nothing about a church wedding, and no idea what the minimum is. Still, they've got 'just the two of you' in the form, so I'll send it and ask.
